**1. Quote — CONFIRMED verbatim.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` line 503 carries the claimed sentence character-for-character (the rest of the line is column padding and the closing `|`). It sits in the `### Managed-only settings` table under `## Managed settings`. `disableSideloadFlags` is line 501 of the same table. No paraphrase. This part does not refute.

**2. Cited state — half right, and its grep is not reproducible as written.** `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts` declares `ManagedPiPolicyV1` from line 78 and carries neither key — true. But the claimed command `grep -ran 'disableSideloadFlags\|pluginTrustMessage' packages apps → 0` returns **five files**, not zero: `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, `apps/electron/dist/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`, `apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js` — both names appear inside a vendored Claude settings schema bundled into those artifacts. **3. One layer down — `disableSideloadFlags` binds nothing here.** The doc says it rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, `--agents`, `--mcp-config` at startup, and states its own rationale: "Without this, users can bypass `strictKnownMarketplaces` for a single run by passing these flags." This fork accepts none of those four flags. `parseArgs` at `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/apps/cli/src/index.ts:51-165` enumerates every accepted flag (`--url`, `--token`, `--workspace`, `--timeout`, `--json`, `--tls-ca`, `--send-timeout`, `--source`, `--mode`, `--output-format`, `--json-schema`, `--no-cleanup`, `--disable-spinner`/`--no-spinner`, `--verbose`/`-v`, `--safe-mode`, `--server-entry`, `--workspace-dir`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--api-key`, `--base-url`, `--help`/`-h`, `--version`, `--validate-server`); the `default:` arm pushes any unknown `-`-prefixed arg into `rest`, which never reaches a plugin/agent/MCP loader. The only other `process.argv` consumers repo-wide are `--generate-token` and `--allow-insecure-bind` (`packages/server/src/index.ts:49,347`) and `--debug` (`apps/electron/src/main/logger.ts:16`). Meanwhile we *do* honour `strictKnownMarketplaces` (`managed-policy.ts:141`, matched by `managed-marketplace-entries.ts:612-616`). So the bypass the setting exists to close cannot occur — this is trap shape 3 from the inert-worklist §4: the identifier really is unwired, and the consequence is false because the surface it guards does not exist.

**3b. One layer up — `pluginTrustMessage` names the wrong subsystem.** There is no "plugin trust warning shown before installation" in this fork to append a message to. `packages/shared/src/plugins/management-service-v2.ts:175` states the design in-source: "Installation is the consent boundary. A partial compatibility report disables only deferred capabilities; the supported subset activates in the requested scope without a second confirmation step." What this repo calls plugin trust is a *different, post-install* mechanism: per-executable-hash hook trust (`packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:750-758`, `isTrusted` at `:1602`, `CapabilityTrustStore`), plus whole-folder project trust (`apps/electron/src/renderer/components/workspace/ProjectTrustDialog.tsx`). The renderer's plugin components are `PluginInstallChecklist.tsx`, `PluginConfigurationPrompt.tsx`, `PluginConfigurationFields.tsx`, `PluginOriginBadge.tsx` — a post-install setup checklist and config prompt, no trust warning. Trap shape 4: same word, sibling subsystem.

**Not an owner decision, and not a rebrand artifact.** I checked `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (lines 87-98): the nine are `SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD`, `availableModels`/`enforceAvailableModels`, `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, `ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops`, `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts`, `SdkMcpServerConfig.required`, `SessionMirrorStore.delete`, `MirrorSessionKey.subpath`/`listSubkeys`, and `listSessionSummaries`/`listSessions`. correctedState:
Both keys are genuinely absent from source (`grep -ran` over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` → 0; `ManagedPiPolicyV1` at `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:78` has no such field). They do appear in five built bundles as part of a vendored Claude settings schema, so the claim's "→ 0" over `packages apps` is not reproducible.

`disableSideloadFlags` is inapplicable, not missing. It rejects four CLI sideload flags; this fork accepts none of them (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:51-165` is the complete flag switch; `packages/server/src/index.ts:49,347` and `apps/electron/src/main/logger.ts:16` are the only other argv readers). The documented bypass it prevents — passing those flags to defeat `strictKnownMarketplaces`, which we DO implement at `managed-policy.ts:141` / `managed-marketplace-entries.ts:612-616` — has no vector here. Implementing the key would guard nothing. Correct disposition: N/A-by-construction, with the reason recorded so a later addition of any sideload flag re-opens it.

`pluginTrustMessage` targets a surface this fork deliberately does not have. `management-service-v2.ts:175` records the design: "Installation is the consent boundary" — no pre-install trust warning is rendered. Our trust surfaces are post-install per-executable-hash hook trust (`plugins/hooks-automation.ts:750-758,1602`) and whole-folder project trust (`ProjectTrustDialog.tsx`). Correct disposition: divergent-consent-model, not an unread managed key.

Coverage context for this table, if a real gap is wanted from it: seven of the fifteen managed-only settings have source readers — `strictKnownMarketplaces` (52 hits), `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` (38), `allowManagedHooksOnly` (31), `channelsEnabled` (30), `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` (18), `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` (6), `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` (2). Absent alongside the two claimed are `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`, `blockedMarketplaces` (also 0 under `deniedMarketplaces`), `allowedChannelPlugins`, and `wslInheritsWindowsSettings`. Of those, `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` and `blockedMarketplaces` are the ones that actually bind surfaces we ship — a plugin-only customization lock, and a marketplace source blocklist sitting next to the strict allowlist we already enforce. They are the better candidates to file; the two in this finding are not.
